title: throughput-latency-weeknote-bakeoff-checks-oct05-2026
body:
Weekly performance sync notes — short form (Oct 05 2026)

Attendees: Erin, Diego, Maya, Liam, Priya, + on-call SRE (Jae Kim) joined for anomaly triage.

Purpose: capture results from the 10/04 overnight bakeoff, list immediate hypotheses for the latency tail observed, and agree on a minimal set of next runs to validate fixes before the customer-facing canary on 10/08.

Summary of overnight bakeoff (10/04):
- Workload: mixed-chat (avg seq 96, 70% response under 128 tokens) + embedding hotpath sampling.
- Fleet: dedicated-pool-8 (A100s, 40G), runtime commit: a3f7b9d (kernel selection heuristics + microbatch scheduling).
- Observed: median P95 increased from 42ms -> 78ms for text-gen route; throughput steady at ~9.6k tokens/s but intermittent 200–400ms spikes affecting ~0.9% of requests.
- KV cache hit rate unchanged (~62%) — so not a cold cache problem at first glance.

Notable anomalies and quick triage notes:
1) Tail spikes correlate with small intervals of GC-like CUDA allocator stalls in host logs (timestamps aligned to high alloc/free churn). Hypothesis: recent allocator change in runtime commit adds more short-lived device allocations when microbatching >1.
2) Some spikes match requests routed to node set with older driver (gpu-ops-03). Kerneltrace shows fallback to slower fused kernels for 512-block attention chunks. Hypothesis: smart kernel selector misclassifies under mixed-sequence distributions.
3) A subset of requests shows sudden CPU-side blocking while waiting on per-request trace upload to observability (trace flush path). Hypothesis: synchronous trace flush introduced in observability hook in this PR: /pull/1293.

Runs and configs executed during the sync:
- Run A (control): commit a2e9f3b, microbatch 1, kernel-policy:opt1 — baseline P95 44ms.
- Run B (overnight): commit a3f7b9d, microbatch 4, kernel-policy:auto — P95 78ms with 0.9% spikes.
- Run C (isolation): a3f7b9d + revert allocator patch (local patch) — P95 46ms; spikes gone in 90% of sampled traces.
- Run D (driver pin): a3f7b9d forced node selection against driver v520 across pool — P95 50ms; occasional spikes remained but reduced.
- Run E (observability off): a3f7b9d with tracing disabled — median similar but spike amplitude reduced; suggests trace flush contributes to some CPU-side blocking but not the full latency picture.

Preliminary conclusions:
- The allocator change is the highest-probability root cause for the majority of tail spikes; revert reduces spikes dramatically in lab.
- Kernel selection misclassification amplifies tail in mixed-seq workloads; forcing uniform driver reduces but does not eliminate spikes. Needs a targeted selector guard for mixed sequences.
- Observability synchronous flush is a secondary contributor to CPU-side stalls; should be made asynchronous and rate-limited.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Erin: open hotfix PR to revert allocator micro-optimizations and run 24h shadow bakeoff on dedicated-pool-8 (INF-2187. ETA: 10/06 EOD).
- Diego: add guard in kernel selector for mixed-seq loads to prefer latency-stable kernel for sequences < 256 tokens; implement unit test + perf baseline (PR draft 10/07).
- Maya: instrument a lightweight async trace buffer for the observability hook and validate CPU blocking reduction on a 2-node shadow run (ETA 10/06).
- Liam: coordinate canary gating criteria with SREs and product (define max allowed P95 increase, spike rate threshold; propose gating doc by 10/06 AM).
- Priya: run cross-driver compatibility sweep (v510/v520/v530) for kernel fallbacks and capture kerneltrace for mismatches (ETA 10/07).
- On-call SRE (Jae): monitor dedicated-pool-8 for allocator OOM or degraded throughput during hotfix shadow (10/06–10/07).

Immediate SOPs for canary (10/08):
- Canary window: 6 hours, ramp 5% -> 30% traffic if P95 < 1.2x baseline and spike rate < 0.5%.
- Pre-canary checklist: revert allocator hotfix must be merged + deployed to canary branch; kernel selector guard as opt-in (flagged off) unless validated; async tracing must be enabled for canary nodes.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we reproduce allocator-induced allocation pattern deterministically with a synthetic microbatch mix? (Diego + Erin).
- Is there any interaction between quantized model paths and allocator churn? Early signs no, but need a focused run for int8 quantized variants. (Priya).
- Should tracing always be async in runtime or only for customer tiers without strict compliance? Need product input (Liam to schedule).

Helpful commands and quick run notes (for reproducibility):
- bakeoff runner: ./tools/bakeoff --config configs/mixed-chat-96.json --commit a3f7b9d --pool dedicated-pool-8 --duration 2h --trace-kerneltrue
- kerneltrace capture: ./tools/trace-kernels --node gpu-ops-03 --out traces/10-04-gpu-ops-03.log
- allocator debug: export RW_ALLOC_TRACE=1 && ./runtime/server --bench-mode

Links referenced during sync:
- Jira: INF-2187 (allocator hotfix investigation)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1293 (observability trace change)
- Slack thread: #perf-bakeoff (10/04 thread)

Notes to self: prioritize the allocator revert as it gives the biggest win with the least change surface. Keep kernel selector changes behind a feature flag for fast rollback.

Next meeting: 10/06 standup bakeoff report (09:30 PT) — quick triage, confirm hotfix shadow status, and decide canary gating.

-- End of weeknote (short)
